silhouette.reason: Now a flatter, wider crown on a long clear bole, the umbrella of an old Scots pine; but in hero.png the crown is a near-rectangular block (flat top, flat bottom, straight sides) on straight horizontal rod limbs, so it reads as a box hedge on a pole rather than separate flat pads.
fixes: break the crown into 2–3 separate flat pads with sky gaps between them
limbs that kink and turn up toward their tips instead of straight horizontal rods

proportions.reason: 22 m tall with a ~0.9 m bole and an 11.5 m crown: the bole now reads as a trunk, not a pencil, and the crown depth fits an old Scots pine.
fixes: a visible taper from the root flare to the crown base

materials.reason: Needle cards now read feathery and conifer-like at hero distance but stay a dark green; the bark is the orange upper-bole tone right down to the base, where a Scots pine turns grey-brown and plated.
fixes: grey-brown plated bark on the lower third of the bole, orange only above
a lighter blue-green tint on the outer needle tufts

detail.reason: Orange limbs show inside the crown and stubs along the bole; no cones, and the limbs are uniform straight rods.
fixes: branch forks and taper on the limbs

wear.reason: Dead stubs and a pale peeled strip down the lower bole (hero.png) that reads as a flat ribbon more than a scar; no resin.
fixes: give the pale strip raised bark lips and resin at its edges
a dead branch inside the crown

lod.reason: FAR LOD2 crown is still sparser, lighter and more see-through than the LOD0 crown, with the leader exposed above it.
fixes: denser LOD2 pad cards colour-matched to LOD0
spend a few more LOD2 triangles on crown cards
